decisions.question: core-wide sampler fixes keep re-opening rows that already have a valid demo — keep re-running everything, or freeze valid rows against blanket fixes?
decisions.context: Today: ontop_small, under_small, nextto and inside turned valid on 6b856ed (18:35–19:06) and were re-opened 19:25 by the core's two-tier grasp draw 02c700d (4 subtasks in one entry); earlier bcc1478 / 625759b / dc6a1a5 did the same to object_scaling, mental_rotation, axial, disembedding. Each flip costs ~4 pod-hours and the board oscillates (9/21 → 6/21). The rule as written (06:50): a demo is valid only if its code carries every fix affecting the subtask.
options: A) keep the rule as is — every affecting fix re-runs the subtask (current behaviour, maximal guarantee)

B) freeze: a row with a valid demo is re-run only by a fix targeted at it (≤ 5 subtasks) or on your RUN:; blanket entries mark it 'valid (pre-<sha>)' and the final validity sweep happens once at the end of the pass
C) B, plus agents batch core-wide changes (≤ 1 per hour) — I have already asked the core to batch
decisions.default: A until you answer (the runs are already scheduled); C is my recommendation
decisions.answer: C - freeze valid rows against blanket fixes (targeted fix = < 6 subtasks, or RUN:), blanket entries mark valid (pre-<sha>), one final validity sweep at the end of the pass; agents batch core-wide changes (<= 1 per hour)

decisions.question: the last block of the 2×2 grid cannot be pinched into 1 mm gaps (two occupied sides) — widen the gaps to 6 mm, or let the oracle push the last block into place?

decisions.question: the teacup lands correctly on the saucer but OmniGibson's Under predicate sometimes never turns true — make the evaluator robust, fall back to a pose target, or keep re-running?
decisions.context: Core (20:25): the 20:xx re-run on 02c700d placed the cup 1.4 mm from the goal, 2.7° tilt, centred on the saucer well (release 6.5 mm above the well floor, straight carry), yet (under saucer teacup) was never true (binary_success_ever False) — the same geometry passed at 18:41. OmniGibson's Under shoots a ray up from the saucer's own well-floor surface into the resting cup's bottom; whether it registers depends on sub-mm contact/penetration. The release also spun the cup 0.27 rad in yaw (> 0.20 orientation tolerance), so a pose target would need the yaw relaxed (cups are yaw-symmetric).
options: A) evaluator: robust Under for concave partners — several rays across the contact patch, ray origin a few mm below the partner's top surface, any hit counts (applies to every under task, policy evaluation included)
B) pose-target fallback for under-small: position within tolerance + up-axis within 15° counts as success when the predicate ray misses (yaw relaxed for yaw-symmetric targets)
C) leave it: re-run until the predicate registers (18:41 passed; ~1 pod-hour per attempt, flaky policy evaluation later)
decisions.default: A at 21:15 PDT if unanswered (evaluator change, logged for every under subtask; B not applied)
decisions.answer: default A applied: robust under/ontop wrapper ispatialgym.sampling.predicates.evaluate_predicate (OmniGibson -> contact-patch rays -> geometry; deciding branch logged as meta.binary_branch / goal_check.binary_branch), shared by the sampler goal check and the task evaluator
